The Battle of San Jacinto was fought on 21 April 1836 beside the San Jacinto River, near today's Houston in Texas, United States. A Texan army under Sam Houston surprised and destroyed a Mexican army led by the president of Mexico, General Antonio López de Santa Anna. The fighting lasted about 18 minutes.

Texas was then part of Mexico, settled largely by people from the United States. In 1835 they rebelled against Santa Anna's central government, and in March 1836 they declared independence. Santa Anna marched north, stormed the Alamo and had several hundred prisoners shot at Goliad. Houston retreated east for weeks while settlers fled. Then Santa Anna split his army and Houston turned on him. In the afternoon, while the Mexican camp rested, about 900 Texans charged across the open field shouting "Remember the Alamo!" About 630 Mexican soldiers were killed and over 700 captured. The Texans lost fewer than a dozen men.

Santa Anna was caught the next day and signed an order pulling his troops out of Texas. Texas became an independent republic, though Mexico never accepted it. In 1845 it joined the United States, which led straight to the Mexican-American War.
